guides.title: Entry price versus quoted price
guides.concept: A displayed quote is an observation, while entry price is the confirmed average fill of an executed order.
guides.prerequisites: Understand bids, asks, orders, fills, timestamps, and share-weighted averages.
guides.procedure: Record the decision-time quote, order instructions, each fill, shares, fees, and timestamps; compute the share-weighted fill separately from the quote.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 60 shares fill at $10.04 and 40 at $10.10; average entry=(60×10.04+40×10.10)/100=$10.064.
guides.limit: The example excludes fees and does not claim the displayed quote was executable for all shares.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when fill quantities, fill prices, order status, timestamp, or fee treatment is missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Recording the $10.00 screen quote as the entry hides six-point-four cents of execution difference. Correct with confirmed fill records.
guides.selfCheck: Which record establishes entry cost: the observed quote or the completed fills?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: entry cost comes from confirmed fills. The fictional weighted calculation produces $10.064, not the screen quote. Missing fills or fees block a final cost claim. No order or grade is created.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 30 shares fill at $8.20 and 70 at $8.26; compute average entry and name one missing cost.

sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: The example excludes fees and does not claim the displayed quote was executable for all shares. guides.title: Cumulative partial-fill reconciliation
guides.concept: A partial fill creates an executed position and a separate unfilled remainder; neither should be mistaken for the original order size.
guides.prerequisites: Understand order quantity, filled quantity, open quantity, cancellation, and duplicate-order risk.
guides.procedure: Read cumulative filled shares from the broker record, subtract once from ordered shares, and verify whether the remainder is open, canceled, or rejected.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A 500-share order fills 180 shares; 500−180=320 shares remain only if the order is still open.
guides.limit: The remainder can change with later fills or cancellation acknowledgments.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when cumulative versus incremental fills or current order status cannot be distinguished.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Submitting another 500 shares after a partial fill can create 680 total shares. Correct by reconciling cumulative fills and open quantity first.
guides.selfCheck: Why is remaining quantity conditional on current order status?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: subtract the cumulative fill once, then verify status. Fictional remaining quantity is 320 only while open. No replacement order is recommended.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: A 750-share order has 275 cumulative fills; calculate the possible open remainder and state the status check required.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: Cumulative partial-fill reconciliation: SEC explains partially executed orders and unfilled remainder. This is a contextual reference for original fictional instruction, not endorsement of its example.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: The remainder can change with later fills or cancellation acknowledgments. Verify actual source-to-claim match, formula conventions, broker/issuer context, data provenance, publication and redistribution rights with an independent reviewer.

guides.title: Limit-order price protection
guides.concept: A buy limit sets the highest acceptable price but does not guarantee execution.
guides.prerequisites: Understand buy and sell orders, bids, asks, price priority, and unfilled orders.
guides.procedure: State side, limit, quantity, duration, observed market, and final status; separate acceptable price from execution certainty.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A buy limit of $24.50 while the ask is $24.70 remains unfilled; the limit protects price but supplies no fill.
guides.limit: Queue position, available size, venue rules, and later prices are unknown.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when side, limit price, order status, or market timestamp is unavailable.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Treating a touched limit as a guaranteed fill ignores queue and available liquidity. Correct by checking confirmed executions.
guides.selfCheck: What does a buy limit guarantee, and what does it not guarantee?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: the fictional limit caps acceptable purchase price but creates no execution promise. Only a fill confirms a position.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: A sell limit is $31.20 while the bid is $31.05; describe protection and the unresolved outcome.

guides.title: Stop trigger versus fill price
guides.concept: A stop trigger activates an order; it is not necessarily the eventual execution price.
guides.prerequisites: Understand trigger conditions, market orders, gaps, liquidity, and fill confirmation.
guides.procedure: Record stop type and trigger, the first eligible triggering observation, resulting order type, and actual fills without substituting the trigger for a fill.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A sell stop triggers at $15.00 after a gap and fills at $14.72; 100 shares realize $28 more loss than a $15.00 assumption.
guides.limit: Trigger and execution rules vary by order and venue; the example is not a universal broker rule.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when trigger basis, resulting order type, session eligibility, or fills are unknown.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Booking the stop price as guaranteed proceeds understates gap and liquidity risk. Correct with the confirmed fill.
guides.selfCheck: Why can trigger price and fill price differ?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: activation and execution are separate events. Fictional 28-cent difference on 100 shares equals $28. No future fill is promised.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: A stop triggers at $9.40 and 200 shares fill at $9.31; compute the trigger-to-fill difference in dollars.

guides.title: Position size from risk budget
guides.concept: Risk-based share size divides a declared dollar-risk budget by planned risk per share, then rounds down to a permitted whole-share amount.
guides.prerequisites: Understand entry, invalidation level, per-share risk, account risk budget, and execution uncertainty.
guides.procedure: Compute absolute entry-to-invalidation distance, reject zero or negative distance, divide budget by distance, round down, then test fees and slippage separately.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: $120 risk budget and $0.75 planned risk per share give floor(120/0.75)=160 shares before costs.
guides.limit: A planned stop cannot cap realized loss during gaps, halts, or failed execution.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when entry, invalidation level, budget, currency, or permitted share increment is missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Dividing by entry price sizes capital, not planned loss. Correct by using entry-to-invalidation distance.
guides.selfCheck: Which denominator connects share quantity to the stated loss budget?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional risk size is 160 shares before costs. The result is a planning ceiling, not guaranteed realized loss.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Risk budget $95 and planned distance $0.60; calculate the whole-share ceiling and unused budget.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: CME describes risk-based size from planned stop distance and account risk; 160 shares is an independent whole-share fictional case.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: CME examples cover contracts and stop references; stock whole-share size, gaps, fees and broker rules require separate validation. Independently verify exact claim support, URL stability, arithmetic, publication and third-party rights before release.

guides.title: Portfolio heat from open planned risk
guides.concept: Portfolio heat aggregates declared remaining planned risk across open positions, not their market values.
guides.prerequisites: Understand position-level risk, stop assumptions, correlated exposure, and account equity.
guides.procedure: For each open position compute shares times remaining entry-to-invalidation distance, sum comparable currencies, and divide by current equity if a percentage is needed.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Open risks of $90, $140, and $70 total $300; against $20,000 equity, planned heat is 1.5%.
guides.limit: Correlation, gaps, slippage, and stop failures can make realized loss exceed summed planned risk.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when any position lacks quantity, risk level, currency conversion, or current account equity.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Adding position market values and calling the sum risk confuses exposure with planned loss. Correct by declaring the risk method.
guides.selfCheck: Why can equal market values contribute different portfolio heat?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional planned risk sums to $300 and 1.5% of equity. This remains conditional on execution assumptions.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Risks are $45, $85, and $110 against $16,000 equity; compute heat and name one omitted risk.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: Risk per position is stop distance × size; open portfolio heat is the sum of non-negative planned stop losses divided by equity.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: Portfolio-heat label is an educational convention; specify initial versus current stop and do not treat stop-based risk as maximum actual loss. Secondary source is practitioner context, not an independent professional certification. Independently verify exact claim support, URL stability, arithmetic, publication and third-party rights before release.

guides.title: Scale-in weighted average cost
guides.concept: Adding shares changes average cost according to share weights, not the simple average of fill prices.
guides.prerequisites: Understand fills, quantities, weighted means, fees, and position reconciliation.
guides.procedure: Multiply each fill price by its shares, sum notionals, divide by total filled shares, and keep fees in a declared separate or included convention.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 100 shares at $12 and 50 at $13 produce ($1,200+$650)/150=$12.3333 average before fees.
guides.limit: Average cost says nothing about whether adding exposure improved the decision.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when fill quantities, prices, canceled shares, or fee convention is incomplete.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Averaging $12 and $13 to $12.50 ignores unequal share weights. Correct with fill notional divided by shares.
guides.selfCheck: Why is the simple mean wrong when fill sizes differ?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional weighted cost is about $12.33, not $12.50. The calculation evaluates records, not trade quality.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 40 shares at $20 and 160 at $19.50; compute weighted average before fees.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: Scale-in weighted average cost: SEC documents partial fills at different prices, not a strategy endorsement. This is a contextual reference for original fictional instruction, not endorsement of its example.

guides.title: Scale-out realized and open quantity
guides.concept: A partial exit realizes results only on exited shares while leaving a separately measured open quantity.
guides.prerequisites: Understand position quantity, exit fills, realized versus unrealized results, and cost-basis conventions.
guides.procedure: Reconcile starting shares, subtract confirmed exit shares, calculate realized result under the declared basis, and leave open shares unclosed.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: From 300 shares at $10, selling 120 at $10.80 realizes $96 before costs and leaves 180 shares open.
guides.limit: Tax-lot and broker cost-basis rules may differ from the simplified single-basis example.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when original lots, exit fills, quantity, fees, or basis method is missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Applying the $0.80 gain to all 300 shares overstates realized profit. Correct by using only exited shares.
guides.selfCheck: Which shares contribute to realized result after a partial exit?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: only 120 exited shares create fictional $96 realized profit; 180 remain exposed.

guides.title: Break-even with round-trip costs
guides.concept: Economic break-even must recover declared entry and exit costs in addition to the entry price.
guides.prerequisites: Understand shares, commissions, regulatory fees, spread, slippage, and per-share allocation.
guides.procedure: Sum declared round-trip costs, divide by shares, add cost per share to entry for a long position, and label omitted variable costs.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 200 shares entered at $25 with $8 declared round-trip costs require $25.04 per share to break even before omitted costs.
guides.limit: Future exit fees and slippage are estimates until the exit fills.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when share count, entry fills, cost scope, currency, or anticipated exit convention is absent.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling $25.00 break-even ignores $8 of friction. Correct by allocating declared round-trip cost over shares.
guides.selfCheck: Why does break-even depend on both cost scope and share count?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: $8 divided by 200 is $0.04, so fictional break-even is $25.04 under the stated cost scope.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 500 shares enter at $6.40 with $15 declared round-trip costs; compute simplified break-even.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: Break-even with round-trip costs: SEC investor fees resource explains transaction costs and break-even. This is a contextual reference for original fictional instruction, not endorsement of its example.

guides.title: R-multiple realized outcome
guides.concept: An R-multiple divides a consistently measured realized result by the trade's declared initial dollar risk.
guides.prerequisites: Understand initial risk, realized net result, costs, sign conventions, and nonzero denominators.
guides.procedure: Freeze initial planned risk before outcome, compute realized net result under a declared cost convention, and divide by positive initial risk.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Initial risk $150 and realized net profit $225 produce +1.5R.
guides.limit: R standardizes the stated trade result but does not establish strategy expectancy or skill.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when initial risk was not recorded before outcome, equals zero, or result and risk use inconsistent cost treatment.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Replacing initial risk with a later tightened stop inflates R. Correct by preserving the pre-trade denominator.
guides.selfCheck: Why must initial R be frozen before the outcome is known?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: $225 divided by $150 equals +1.5R. Changing the denominator afterward creates hindsight bias.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Initial risk $80 and net loss $52; compute signed R and state one interpretation limit.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: The Van Tharp Institute explicitly defines R-multiple as realized gain/loss divided by initial planned risk; original 225/150=1.5R arithmetic.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: Record gross-versus-net gain convention and treatment of fees. Van Tharp teaching content is reference-only, not licensed for republishing. Independently verify exact claim support, URL stability, arithmetic, publication and third-party rights before release.

guides.title: Maximum adverse excursion
guides.concept: Maximum adverse excursion is the largest unfavorable marked move during a defined holding interval, measured from a declared reference.
guides.prerequisites: Understand long versus short signs, entry reference, intratrade timestamps, raw data, and completed holding intervals.
guides.procedure: Freeze direction and entry reference, inspect only eligible observations between entry and exit, calculate each adverse move, and retain the largest magnitude.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Long entry $30; lowest eligible trade before exit is $29.25, so price MAE is $0.75 or 2.5% of entry.
guides.limit: Bar lows can overstate executable adverse fills and omit intrabar path.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when entry, direction, holding interval, observation granularity, or corporate-action state is missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Using a low printed after exit introduces lookahead. Correct by enforcing the holding cutoff.
guides.selfCheck: Which time boundary determines eligible MAE observations?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional adverse move is $0.75 and 2.5% within the holding interval. It is a path statistic, not a fill claim.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Long entry $16, eligible low $15.52; compute price and percentage MAE.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: Maximum adverse excursion: QuantConnect backtest statistics describes maximum adverse excursion. This is a contextual reference for original fictional instruction, not endorsement of its example.

guides.title: Maximum favorable excursion
guides.concept: Maximum favorable excursion is the largest favorable marked move inside the holding interval and is not necessarily achievable profit.
guides.prerequisites: Understand direction, entry reference, eligible highs or lows, timestamps, and execution limits.
guides.procedure: Freeze direction and entry, restrict evidence to the holding interval, compute favorable moves, and retain the maximum without treating it as an executed exit.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Long entry $12.50; highest eligible trade is $13.40, so price MFE is $0.90 or 7.2%.
guides.limit: Observed extremes do not prove sufficient size was executable at that price.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when interval, direction, reference, feed scope, or eligible extreme is uncertain.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling the session high missed profit when it occurred after exit fabricates opportunity. Correct with holding-time eligibility.
guides.selfCheck: Why is MFE not the same as realizable profit?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional favorable excursion is $0.90 or 7.2%; no claim is made that the high could be filled.

guides.title: Time stop and elapsed market minutes
guides.concept: A time stop uses a predeclared elapsed-time rule and an exchange-session calendar, not wall-clock intuition.
guides.prerequisites: Understand entry timestamps, trading sessions, halts, time zones, and order execution.
guides.procedure: Declare whether elapsed time means wall minutes or eligible market minutes, identify pauses and session boundaries, then compare completed elapsed time with the rule.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Entry 10:05, rule 30 wall minutes, evaluation 10:35: the time condition is met, but exit still requires an executable order.
guides.limit: A time condition does not guarantee an immediate fill and may require special handling for halts.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when time zone, timestamp, halt treatment, or elapsed-time convention is unspecified.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Counting overnight hours as regular-session minutes changes the rule. Correct by using the declared calendar convention.
guides.selfCheck: Which elapsed-time convention governs the decision?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: the fictional 30-minute condition is met at 10:35, but the lesson does not invent an exit fill.

guides.title: Trailing reference without lookahead
guides.concept: A trailing reference may use only completed observations available before the current decision cutoff.
guides.prerequisites: Understand rolling highs or lows, completed bars, update timing, and stop triggers.
guides.procedure: Declare window, completion rule, update cadence, and cutoff; calculate the reference from the eligible prefix and freeze it before testing the next observation.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Completed lows are $20.10, $20.25, $20.40; a rule using the lowest of those references $20.10 before the next bar.
guides.limit: A reference level is not a guaranteed exit price.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when the window includes the current incomplete bar, timestamps are missing, or adjustment state changes.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Including the next bar's low tightens the reference with future evidence. Correct by computing from the prior completed prefix.
guides.selfCheck: Which observations are eligible when a trailing level is set?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional reference is $20.10 from completed evidence only. Trigger and fill remain separate.

guides.title: Gap risk and position loss
guides.concept: When price jumps across a planned exit level, realized loss depends on the eventual fill rather than the skipped level.
guides.prerequisites: Understand prior close, next eligible quote or trade, stop activation, position direction, and fills.
guides.procedure: Record planned level separately, identify the first eligible post-gap execution, calculate result from actual fill, and disclose omitted costs.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 150-share long enters $22 with planned exit $21.50 but fills after a gap at $20.90; gross loss=(22−20.90)×150=$165.
guides.limit: The example does not predict gap frequency or guarantee any particular execution sequence.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when position size, entry fill, exit fill, session, or corporate action status is unknown.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Capping loss at $75 from the planned level ignores the skipped price. Correct with confirmed execution.
guides.selfCheck: Which price determines realized gap loss?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional actual fill creates $165 gross loss; the planned $21.50 level was not an executed price.

guides.title: Halt exposure in an open position
guides.concept: During a halt, the last trade is stale evidence and an open position retains uncertain reopening-price risk.
guides.prerequisites: Understand halts, last trades, quotes, order status, reopening, and position exposure.
guides.procedure: Freeze the last eligible pre-halt information, classify orders by confirmed status, avoid assigning a reopen price, and wait for official reopening evidence.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 200 shares remain long when trading halts after a $9.60 last trade; no reopen quote is supplied, so current executable value is unknown.
guides.limit: Halt reasons, reopening mechanisms, and order handling vary and require venue or broker confirmation.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when the official halt status, position quantity, order status, or reopening timestamp is unavailable.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Marking the position safely exited at a resting stop invents a transaction during the halt. Correct by requiring a fill.

guides.title: Short-position borrow cost
guides.concept: A short trade's net result can include time-dependent borrow charges in addition to price movement and commissions.
guides.prerequisites: Understand short sales, borrowed shares, annualized rates, day-count conventions, and broker-specific charges.
guides.procedure: Use only broker-disclosed principal basis, rate, accrual dates, and day-count method; calculate an estimate and reconcile it with actual posted charges.

guides.title: Short-squeeze risk is not a signal
guides.concept: Short interest and rising price can describe risk conditions but cannot prove that a squeeze will occur or identify participant intent.
guides.prerequisites: Understand short interest, float estimates, covering, borrow constraints, and observation versus inference.
guides.procedure: Timestamp short-interest and float sources, calculate only compatible ratios, label price action separately, and state competing explanations.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Reported short interest 4 million and dated float estimate 20 million imply 20%, but no future covering demand is known.
guides.limit: Reporting lags, float uncertainty, derivatives, and intraperiod position changes limit inference.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when dates, security class, float methodology, or reporting scope do not align.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling a 20% ratio a guaranteed squeeze converts a lagged statistic into a prediction. Correct by treating it as one risk input.
guides.selfCheck: What does the ratio measure, and what future event does it not establish?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional dated ratio is 20%; it neither proves a squeeze nor reveals motives.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Short interest 1.5 million and compatible float 12 million; compute the ratio and give an alternative explanation for a price rise.

guides.title: Correlated positions and shared risk
guides.concept: Different ticker symbols may respond to the same factor, so symbol count alone can understate shared exposure.
guides.prerequisites: Understand sectors, factors, return intervals, correlation, position direction, and estimation uncertainty.
guides.procedure: Define a common return interval, inspect business and factor overlap, calculate correlation only from sufficient aligned data, and stress shared adverse scenarios.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Three equal long positions all lose 4% when a shared sector shock occurs; three tickers did not create three independent outcomes.
guides.limit: Historical correlation is unstable and does not specify future joint losses.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when return windows, timestamps, corporate actions, or factor classifications are incompatible.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling three symbols diversified ignores common drivers. Correct by evaluating factor and scenario concentration.
guides.selfCheck: Why can symbol variety fail to reduce risk?

guides.title: Daily loss-limit state
guides.concept: A daily loss limit requires a fixed reset time, included-result convention, and fail-closed response when records are incomplete.
guides.prerequisites: Understand realized and unrealized results, fees, account time zones, open positions, and risk governance.
guides.procedure: Declare reset boundary and included components before trading, aggregate verified results once, compare with the limit, and block new risk if state is uncertain.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Realized −$180, declared included fees −$20, and limit −$200 place the account exactly at its limit.
guides.limit: Whether unrealized loss counts is a policy choice that must be fixed in advance.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when fills, fees, time zone, reset boundary, or inclusion policy is unavailable.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Excluding fees after reaching the threshold changes the rule to permit more risk. Correct with the predeclared convention.
guides.selfCheck: Which policy choices must be frozen before computing daily loss?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional included loss is exactly $200, so the stated limit is reached. No trading instruction is issued.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Realized −$135 and included fees −$15 against a −$175 limit; compute remaining buffer and one state that should force HOLD.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: CME trade-plan self-evaluation explicitly includes a daily total-dollar loss limit; fictional realized loss plus fees reaches the declared threshold.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: A personal educational loss-state rule is not a broker-enforced shutoff, margin rule or exchange circuit breaker; account P&L inclusion rules must be defined. Independently verify exact claim support, URL stability, arithmetic, publication and third-party rights before release.
